blocks.value: A try block wraps code that might throw an exception. A catch block right after it handles a specific exception type if one is thrown.
A program can only have one try block per try structure, but that try can be followed by multiple catch blocks, each handling a different exception type:
Call getMessage() on a caught exception to see Java's own description of what went wrong: System.out.println(exceptionName.getMessage());
An optional finally block can follow the catch blocks. Its code always runs, whether or not an exception was thrown, which makes it useful for cleanup that has to happen no matter what:
